title: The Wise and Foolish Builders
text:
At the end of the long teaching known as the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus finished with a short story about two men who each built a house.

The first was a wise man. He built his house on rock. Then the rain came down, the streams rose and flooded, and the winds blew and beat against the house. But it did not fall, because its foundation was on the rock.

The second was a foolish man. He built his house on sand. To look at, it may have seemed just as good, and it was certainly easier and quicker to build. Then the same rain came down, the streams rose, and the winds blew and beat against that house. It fell, and its fall was great.

Jesus said that whoever heard his words and put them into practice was like the wise builder, and whoever heard them but did not act on them was like the foolish one. Matthew records that when he finished speaking, the crowds were astonished at his teaching, because he taught as one who had authority. In Luke's shorter version of the same story, the wise builder digs deep before laying his foundation.
lesson: Storms will test every plan, career and relationship. Put the slow, unseen work into foundations now, because by the time the flood comes, it is too late to dig.
location: Galilee and Judea (modern Israel and Palestinian territories)
